scope: Deterministic collaboration integration and comparison design; no product behavior change
actualPath: Two real Role instances in one temporary Kernel database, each with its own execution lane
One Human @all opening, both executions bound to that same sequence
Real MultiLaneAgentHost with FakeRuntimeAdapter supplying synthetic native text
Worker message-present HTTP, nativeFinalSequence/envelope, WorkerFinalOutput HTTP, actual Host settlement
Real Human Client HTTP abandon, followed by an explicit new request
observations: B completes and publishes while A still owns its lane.
B's undirected top-level reply alone makes A's later final held. There is no intervening Human message.
A does not silently publish stale text, ACK unseen peer facts or automatically retry; action_required requires Human recovery.
After Human abandon plus a new request, A receives the peer fact and publishes the exact synthetic @B text once. The test does not add recipients to that reply.
B receives the handoff; its subsequent directed request contains only the new delta, not the old opening or handoff.
The failed RunAttempt remains unchanged. The whole chain has five RunAttempts and four canonical final replies, with no queued or leased work left.

limitRootCause.condition: A newer external message on the same room and exact target (top level or same thread) exceeds the final's genuine causal floor.
limitRootCause.notRequired: An @ to A, a semantic dependency, or a new Human correction
limitRootCause.existingExceptions: Different room/target, system notices, and exact proven writes from A's own current run do not cause this peer-only hold.
limitRootCause.impact: Independent execution lanes do not yet imply smooth parallel ordinary conversation. With native-final enabled, one peer's successful reply can force Human recovery for another. This is a deterministic policy interaction, not evidence of model randomness.

proposedDecisionNotImplemented.recommendation: Consider excluding ordinary peer message appends not explicitly directed to A from the freshness barrier for A's ordinary reply. Keep the actual old basedOnRoomSeq and append at the real current ledger sequence; never backdate or acknowledge unseen messages.
proposedDecisionNotImplemented.tradeoff: Accept explicitly concurrent ordinary replies whose authors have not yet seen one another; preserve later idle delta delivery without adding a model generation solely for publication.
preserve: Human messages and explicitly directed peer requests (including broadcasts targeting A) remain subject to freshness holds
Task, Review, memory and other business-state mutations retain their existing policies
Authentication, membership, execution fencing, idempotency, original read evidence and unknown-write handling
One Kernel policy for Worker and native-final facades; no Host bypass or second queue
proposedDecisionNotImplemented.alternative: A bounded re-read/revision continuation preserves the current freshness rule but costs another model generation and can encounter another newer message. It is not a zero-cost fix and must not reset its retry bound through follow-up Activations. No such continuation was implemented.

limits: Synthetic runtime replies do not establish actual provider parsing, native session continuation, autonomous model cooperation or token efficiency.
The present test proves safe recovery and exposes a usability limitation; passing it does not mean autonomous collaboration is accepted.
The default deployed native-final flags remain unchanged; do not generalize this Human-recovery behavior to every legacy Worker execution mode.
No current Herdr comparative cost claim: this environment is not a Herdr-managed session and no Herdr controls were used.
Existing P89/P92 real collaboration evidence remains valid within its original revisions and modes.
